notes.text: This is a continuation page beginning d’où. The opening calculation passes through the complement expression, a disjoint-sum display, and two displayed Pi pairs. The concluding written equality is Pi_1=Pi_3. The displayed pair indices 1 and 2 were noticed as a mathematical cue, but the distinct two-turn low numeral in the conclusion was not repaired to 2.

Corollaire is struck and underlined, with Proposition written above it. The proposition text contains mutuellement non panachées and an underlined unique. It is followed by the ordered-pair display and the empty-intersection display. The left emphasis marks are two separate strokes. This account describes the source sequence and does not assert an independently established theorem.

The lower passage writes C as the sum of the two Pi objects and the two low omega/w objects, then calls it l’ensemble somme, qui a quatre éléments. It introduces an application canonique and an image set of four signed Sigma entries. The compressed target subscript is unresolved; the first reading fermés is an ink reading, with finies and foncier retained as alternatives.

The final source sentence begins et laquelle and ends at i.e. The crossed t of et was read independently from the surrounding syntax. No continuation beyond this page has been supplied. The labels (18), (19), and the last inline (18) retain earlier-digit material; the earlier 7 in the left label (18) is distinctly separable.

The first pair superscript has a top-like horizontal cap and downward stem, while the second sign has an additional upper arm. This visual comparison led to top as first reading with plus retained. No mathematical interpretation was used to replace the actual drawn form.

No author date, independent title, author page number, explicit author question, or explicit author doubt/check wording was observed. A pencil archive number 34 occurs at the bottom left and is retained only as a TeX comment. No diagram or independent drawing was present. The one source arrow is the arrow of the canonical-application formula.

The annotation X has a horizontal crossing its upper arms, and the proposition’s second Pi has an extra upright. The surviving strokes have been retained with uncertainty covering possible earlier-layer state. No complete older letter has been invented from these remnants. The ordinary complement expression and the nearby Pi index did not authorize suppressing those strokes.
